title: Natural Disasters and the Nonprofit Sector
abstract: arXiv:2609.04136v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: When natural disasters strike, individuals, communities, and even entire countries can suffer. Researchers have studied the impacts of disasters on various factors of interest, from mental health, to poverty, to economic activity. However, the impact of disasters on the nonprofit sector is understudied despite the nonprofit sector's perhaps surprising role in local or national economies as well as its role in disaster response and recovery. Thus, we study the effect of natural disaster damage on different county-level nonprofit outcomes using a panel dataset spanning 1991 to 2021 and causal inference methods tailored to panel data. Contrary to prior work, which found small but positive associations between disaster damage and nonprofit revenue or assets, we find no evidence of a causal effect.

translated_title: 自然灾害与非营利部门
translated_abstract: 当自然灾害来袭时，个人、社区甚至整个国家都可能遭受苦难。研究人员已经研究了灾害对各种相关因素的影响，从心理健康到贫困，再到经济活动。然而，尽管非营利部门在地方或国家经济中扮演着或许令人惊讶的角色，并且在灾害响应与恢复中发挥着重要作用，灾害对非营利部门的影响却一直缺乏充分研究。因此，我们使用涵盖1991年至2021年的面板数据集以及专为面板数据设计的因果推断方法，研究自然灾害损害对县级非营利组织各项结果的影响。与先前发现灾害损害与非营利组织收入或资产之间存在微小但正相关联系的研究相反，我们没有发现任何因果效应的证据。
tldr: 本研究利用1991年至2021年的县级面板数据和因果推断方法，发现自然灾害损害对非营利组织的收入和资产等结果不存在因果影响，推翻了以往观察到的正相关关系。
en_tdlr: Using a county-level panel dataset from 1991 to 2021 and causal inference methods, this study finds no causal effect of natural disaster damage on nonprofit outcomes, contradicting prior work that reported small positive associations.
